procedure: Fill a syringe with water and insert its nozzle into a thin plastic tube.
Press the syringe to fill the tube with water.
Half fill the second syringe with water and insert its nozzle to the other end of the tube.
Press one plunger in through some distance.
Observe whether the second plunger is pushed out through the same distance.
Observe whether the pressure is transmitted to the second plunger by the liquid.
aim: To demonstrate that pressure applied to a liquid is transmitted through the liquid to another plunger.

viva.question: What does Pascal’s law state?
viva.answer: Pressure applied to an enclosed liquid is transmitted undiminished in all directions.

viva.question: What transmits the pressure from one syringe to the other?
viva.answer: The water in the connected tube and syringes.

viva.question: What happens when one plunger is pressed in?
viva.answer: The pressure transmitted through the water pushes the other plunger out.

viva.question: Why should the tube and syringes be filled with water?
viva.answer: So the applied pressure is transmitted through the liquid.

viva.question: What is the SI unit of pressure?

diagram: Draw two syringes connected by a water-filled plastic tube; label the plunger moving out, water, plastic tube, and plunger pressed in.
title: Demonstration of Pascal’s Law
precautions: Make sure the tube is fitted securely to both syringe nozzles.
Fill the tube with water before connecting the second syringe.
Keep the apparatus steady while pressing a plunger.
result: Pressing one plunger transmits pressure through the water and pushes the other plunger out. This demonstrates Pascal’s law.
